investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-15T14:56–15:03Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent pod never left the Pending state, so the expected-output contract was violated in full.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent feature has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the only 2 nodes eligible to run peer-pod workloads. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms that no schedulable capacity exists for new remote-agent pods. Because the pod never became Running, the eval runner in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs (lines 1880–1885) could not complete createAgent() and therefore produced no evidence, causing the contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json (lines 254–259) to fail on all four required fields. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
proof: failed-check.message: scheduler reports '0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector' — pod was Unschedulable for 128s before the check timed out.
failed-check.timing: status=fail, latencyMs=131626, endedAt=2026-07-15T14:58:34.991Z — the check ran to near-timeout without producing any evidence.
failed-check.evidence: evidence object is empty ({}) — no orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState was captured, confirming the pod never reached a schedulable state.
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent, matching the empty evidence object.

sibling.remote-agent-state: identical scheduler error ('2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector'), pod stuck for 147s — confirms the capacity exhaustion persisted across sequential eval runs.
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical scheduler error, pod stuck for 142s — a third independent pod submission also failed to schedule, ruling out a transient single-pod anomaly.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1877-1885: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1885; if the resulting pod is never scheduled, no downstream evidence fields can be written.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf ['running','idle','ready'] — neither assertion can be satisfied when the pod is Pending.
possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource is fully consumed on both eligible nodes — all three independent pod submissions received the same 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' rejection, indicating zero remaining allocatable units on those 2 nodes at the time of the eval run.

[Likely contributing] Node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes — the remote-agent pod spec restricts scheduling to nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource label; those 4 nodes are structurally ineligible regardless of capacity, reducing the effective scheduling pool to 2 nodes.

[Possible] Leaked or zombie peer-pod VMs holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots — if prior remote-agent pods were not cleaned up (e.g., due to a failed withCleanup() call in the runner), their resource reservations would persist and reduce available capacity.

[Possible] Cluster autoscaler has not provisioned additional kata-capable nodes — if the node pool for peer-pod workloads has a fixed size of 2 and autoscaling is disabled or quota-limited, capacity cannot recover automatically.

[Lower confidence] A change in the remote-agent pod spec (resource request quantity or node selector) that increased per-pod consumption or narrowed eligible nodes — no suspect changes are listed in sourceDiscovery.suspectChanges, so this cannot be confirmed from supplied evidence.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe node on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes shows non-zero remaining kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity, the 'Insufficient' message would need an alternative explanation (e.g., a race condition or scheduler bug).

If a re-run of the eval immediately after this failure succeeds and produces all four required evidence fields, the capacity exhaustion was transient and self-resolved, suggesting a brief spike rather than a sustained leak or fixed pool limit.

If the pod spec for remote-agent pods was recently changed to request more kata.peerpods.io/vm units per pod (reducing the number of concurrent pods the 2 nodes can host), that would shift the cause from capacity exhaustion to a configuration change — but no such change appears in sourceDiscovery.suspectChanges.

If the 4 non-matching nodes are shown to have available kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity but are excluded only by node affinity/selector, the root cause would shift to an overly restrictive scheduling constraint rather than raw capacity exhaustion.

If the three failing sibling checks ran concurrently and their pods competed for the same remaining slots, a single-slot exhaustion event could explain all three failures without implying sustained zero capacity — sequential success after the eval run would support this.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval that checks kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity on eligible nodes before attempting remote-agent creation, surfacing a 'capacity-low' warning before the scheduling failure occurs.
Add an eval that counts currently running remote-agent pods and compares against the known kata.peerpods.io/vm pool size, alerting when utilization exceeds a configurable threshold (e.g., 80%).
Add a cleanup-verification eval that confirms no orphaned remote-agent pods remain after each probe run, catching withCleanup() failures before they accumulate into capacity exhaustion.

Add a node-affinity coverage eval that verifies the number of nodes matching the remote-agent pod's node selector/affinity is above a minimum threshold, catching pool shrinkage before it causes scheduling failures.

investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All Three Remote-Agent Checks
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api with identical Kubernetes scheduling errors reporting that 0 of 6 nodes could accept a new pod: 2 nodes have insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because no pod was ever scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call never completed, and the expected evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) were never written, causing the remote-agent-state contract validation to fail with all four required evidence keys missing.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent (kata peer-pods) workload has exhausted its schedulable VM capacity on the two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource. The remaining four nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector rules. With zero eligible nodes available and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote-agent pod creation attempt times out unscheduled. This is an infrastructure-layer resource exhaustion condition localized to the remote-agent VM pool in the production-api environment. It is an eval-detected infrastructure failure; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence to confirm a broader user-facing outage, though the condition would prevent any new remote agent from being provisioned.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource pool exhausted on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes: all available VM slots are occupied by existing remote-agent pods, leaving no room for the eval's probe pod. Preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist.

Secondary — node affinity or node selector misconfiguration: the 4 remaining nodes are excluded by the pod spec's affinity/selector rules, artificially shrinking the schedulable pool to only 2 nodes. If those rules are overly restrictive or were recently tightened, capacity that should be available is invisible to the scheduler.

Tertiary — leaked or zombie remote-agent pods holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots: if prior eval runs or user sessions did not clean up their pods (e.g., withCleanup in the runner failed), VM slots may be occupied by idle pods, reducing available capacity below the threshold needed for new scheduling.

Quaternary — cluster node count reduction: if one or more kata-capable nodes were drained, cordoned, or removed from the pool, the effective VM capacity would drop, causing previously passing evals to fail without any code change.

Because no pod could be scheduled, the createAgent call in the eval runner never completed, no evidence was collected, and all three remote-agent checks failed with Unschedulable status. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence; this is an eval-infrastructure failure against the production-api environment.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-15T14:56–15:03Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent pod never left the Pending state, so the expected-output contract was violated in full.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent feature has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the only 2 nodes eligible to run peer-pod workloads. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms that no schedulable capacity exists for new remote-agent pods. Because the pod never became Running, the eval runner in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs (lines 1880–1885) could not complete createAgent() and therefore produced no evidence, causing the contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json (lines 254–259) to fail on all four required fields. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
proof: failed-check.message: scheduler reports '0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector' — pod was Unschedulable for 128s before the check timed out.
failed-check.timing: status=fail, latencyMs=131626, endedAt=2026-07-15T14:58:34.991Z — the check ran to near-timeout without producing any evidence.
failed-check.evidence: evidence object is empty ({}) — no orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState was captured, confirming the pod never reached a schedulable state.
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent, matching the empty evidence object.

sibling.remote-agent-state: identical scheduler error ('2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector'), pod stuck for 147s — confirms the capacity exhaustion persisted across sequential eval runs.
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical scheduler error, pod stuck for 142s — a third independent pod submission also failed to schedule, ruling out a transient single-pod anomaly.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1877-1885: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1885; if the resulting pod is never scheduled, no downstream evidence fields can be written.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf ['running','idle','ready'] — neither assertion can be satisfied when the pod is Pending.
possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource is fully consumed on both eligible nodes — all three independent pod submissions received the same 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' rejection, indicating zero remaining allocatable units on those 2 nodes at the time of the eval run.

[Likely contributing] Node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes — the remote-agent pod spec restricts scheduling to nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource label; those 4 nodes are structurally ineligible regardless of capacity, reducing the effective scheduling pool to 2 nodes.

[Possible] Leaked or zombie peer-pod VMs holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots — if prior remote-agent pods were not cleaned up (e.g., due to a failed withCleanup() call in the runner), their resource reservations would persist and reduce available capacity.

[Possible] Cluster autoscaler has not provisioned additional kata-capable nodes — if the node pool for peer-pod workloads has a fixed size of 2 and autoscaling is disabled or quota-limited, capacity cannot recover automatically.

[Lower confidence] A change in the remote-agent pod spec (resource request quantity or node selector) that increased per-pod consumption or narrowed eligible nodes — no suspect changes are listed in sourceDiscovery.suspectChanges, so this cannot be confirmed from supplied evidence.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe node on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes shows non-zero remaining kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity, the 'Insufficient' message would need an alternative explanation (e.g., a race condition or scheduler bug).

If a re-run of the eval immediately after this failure succeeds and produces all four required evidence fields, the capacity exhaustion was transient and self-resolved, suggesting a brief spike rather than a sustained leak or fixed pool limit.

If the pod spec for remote-agent pods was recently changed to request more kata.peerpods.io/vm units per pod (reducing the number of concurrent pods the 2 nodes can host), that would shift the cause from capacity exhaustion to a configuration change — but no such change appears in sourceDiscovery.suspectChanges.

If the 4 non-matching nodes are shown to have available kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity but are excluded only by node affinity/selector, the root cause would shift to an overly restrictive scheduling constraint rather than raw capacity exhaustion.

If the three failing sibling checks ran concurrently and their pods competed for the same remaining slots, a single-slot exhaustion event could explain all three failures without implying sustained zero capacity — sequential success after the eval run would support this.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval that checks kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity on eligible nodes before attempting remote-agent creation, surfacing a 'capacity-low' warning before the scheduling failure occurs.
Add an eval that counts currently running remote-agent pods and compares against the known kata.peerpods.io/vm pool size, alerting when utilization exceeds a configurable threshold (e.g., 80%).

investigations.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes Pod Unschedulable Due to Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every attempt to schedule a remote agent pod was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both are at capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence was returned by any check, meaning the agent pod never started and the expected-output contract (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) could not be satisfied.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource across the 2 eligible nodes (0/6 nodes available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector). Because no pod could be scheduled, the createAgent call in the eval runner never completed, no evidence was collected, and all three remote-agent checks failed with Unschedulable status. This is a cluster-capacity or node-resource constraint failure localized to the remote-agents swarm VM pool, not an application code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence; this is an eval-infrastructure failure against the production-api environment.

source-context.infra/evals/status/features.json:181-189: remote-agent-runtime is registered as required=false with outageLatencyMs=420000; the check failed well within that window (148 s), confirming the failure is scheduling-driven, not a latency threshold breach.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: all available VM slots are occupied by existing pods, leaving no capacity for new eval agent pods. Preemption was also ruled out ('No preemption victims found'), meaning no lower-priority pods could be evicted to make room.

Secondary — node affinity or node selector misconfiguration: 4 of 6 nodes do not match the pod's affinity/selector, artificially constraining scheduling to only 2 nodes. If the affinity rules are overly restrictive or point to a stale node label, the effective pool is smaller than intended.

Tertiary — cluster under-provisioning: the total kata.peerpods.io/vm quota across the 2 matching nodes may be too small to absorb concurrent eval runs (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, and remote-agent-runtime all ran within the same ~5-minute window and each required a VM slot).

Lower confidence — transient spike in non-eval workloads consuming VM slots: if production workloads also consume kata.peerpods.io/vm on the same nodes, a traffic spike could temporarily exhaust capacity during the eval window.

affectedAreas.reason: 4 of 6 cluster nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity or selector, artificially limiting the schedulable pool to 2 nodes (failed-check.message).

affectedAreas.reason: All three checks under the remote-agents feature (lines 183-185, source-context.infra/evals/status/features.json:181-189) failed with the same Unschedulable root cause, indicating the entire remote-agents eval surface is blocked by the scheduling constraint.

Review the remote agent pod's node affinity and selector configuration to determine whether the 4 non-matching nodes are intentionally excluded or whether a label or configuration drift has reduced the schedulable pool.

If VM slots are confirmed exhausted, assess whether the cluster needs additional nodes with kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity, or whether the VM quota per node should be increased to accommodate concurrent eval and production workloads.
Check for leaked or stuck remote agent pods from prior eval runs that may be holding VM slots without active workloads; clean up any such pods to restore capacity.

recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Determines whether the 4 non-matching nodes are intentionally excluded or whether label drift has reduced the schedulable pool below its intended size.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe node on the 2 affinity-matching nodes shows kata.peerpods.io/vm slots available (not exhausted), the scheduling-capacity hypothesis would be disproved and a different cause (e.g., pod spec error, admission webhook rejection) would need to be investigated.

If a re-run of the eval immediately after the failure window succeeds and returns all 5 required evidence fields, this would indicate a transient capacity spike rather than a persistent exhaustion or misconfiguration.

If the pod's node affinity/selector rules are found to be intentionally correct and all 4 non-matching nodes are expected to be excluded, the affinity-misconfiguration hypothesis is disproved and the root cause narrows to pure VM slot exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes.
If the Unschedulable message does not recur on a re-run but a different error appears (e.g., image pull failure, OOMKilled, application error), the scheduling layer is not the persistent root cause.

If no other workloads are consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm slots on the eligible nodes at the time of failure, the exhaustion would need to be explained by the eval pods themselves (e.g., prior eval runs leaving leaked pods), which would shift the diagnosis to a cleanup/lifecycle issue.
followUpEvals: Add an eval that directly checks kata.peerpods.io/vm available capacity on each eligible node before attempting agent creation, so scheduling exhaustion is surfaced as a distinct capacity signal rather than a timeout failure.

Add an eval that verifies the count of nodes matching the remote agent pod's affinity/selector is above a minimum threshold, catching node label drift or pool shrinkage before it causes scheduling failures.
Add a cleanup verification eval that confirms no leaked remote agent pods are holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots after each eval run cycle.

Consider a pre-flight scheduling dry-run eval (e.g., using kubectl --dry-run=server) that validates pod schedulability without consuming VM slots, enabling earlier detection of capacity or affinity issues.
